content.overview: Section 56 requires an instrument of transfer, and s. 58 gives an appeal against refusal; transmission operates by law.
content.glance: Section 56 requires an instrument of transfer, and s. 58 gives an appeal against refusal; transmission operates by law.
content.study: A transfer is a voluntary act and needs the prescribed instrument duly stamped and executed, delivered with the certificate. A private company may restrict transfer in its articles, but refusal must follow s. 58 and is appealable to the Tribunal. Transmission arises on death or insolvency and does not need an instrument of transfer. Forged transfers do not defeat the true owner. Rectification of the register lies under s. 59.
